title: Data Minimization Decision Tree
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Organizational Analytics
description: Binary decision tree that guides analysts through four yes or no questions to decide whether a data element should be collected for an organizational analytics project. Includes five sample scenarios with feedback on each answer, hover examples, and a mode for evaluating a data element of the learner's own.

learningObjectives: Justify data collection decisions using the principle of data minimization, distinguishing between necessary and excessive data elements

controls.label: Scenario
controls.description: Choose a sample scenario or Try your own

controls.label: Yes
controls.description: Answer yes to the highlighted question

controls.label: No
controls.description: Answer no to the highlighted question

controls.label: Data element
controls.description: Type a data element to evaluate in Try your own mode

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided decision practice with feedback, followed by independent application
keyQuestions: Is this data element needed for the stated question?
What is the least intrusive form of the data that still answers the question?
How would you justify this decision to the people whose data it is?
commonMisconceptions: Collecting more data is always safer because it might be useful later
Consent alone justifies collecting identifiable data that the question does not need
assessmentOpportunities: Produce a data inventory with a justified outcome for each element
Redesign an analysis question so it can be answered with aggregated data
